### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (soft)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must engage **classical experimental psychology** — perception, memory, learning, color/visual processing, historical perspectives on psychology. Modern social/clinical psychology submissions may be redirected.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Topic mismatch likely results in editorial redirect rather than full peer review.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Modern social / clinical psychology submissions misaligned with classical-experimental scope
- Pure qualitative submissions
- Failure to disclose AI use
- *(community contribution welcome to specify additional Hard Blockers from submission experience)*

### Soft Tax

*(community estimate)* — likely low for classical-experimental tradition authors. Long publication history suggests traditional review cycle; specific timeline data not widely available.

### Best Suited For

- Classical experimental psychology empirical studies
- Visual perception and color perception research
- Memory processes research
- History of psychology / academic perspectives papers
- Traditional psychophysics and perception research
- Authors comfortable with University of Illinois Press classical-psychology venue

### Not Recommended For

- Modern social or clinical psychology (consider JPSP, JCCP)
- Pure qualitative work
- Authors needing rapid turnaround or high citation impact (2-yr citedness 0.32)
- Critical / decolonial psychology

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology General](./journal-of-experimental-psychology-general.md) | If the work is general-experimental psychology with broader implications |
| 2 | [Cognition](../cognitive-science/cognition.md) | If the work has theoretical-cognitive advance |
| 3 | [Review of General Psychology](./review-of-general-psychology.md) | If the work is integrative-historical psychology |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top experimental-psychology venue as "too historical / too classical," The American Journal of Psychology is often a better fit because: it has 130+ years of classical-experimental tradition; history-of-psychology pieces are a distinctive strength; and the venue prestige (h-index 346) provides a traditional-psychology citation outlet.
